messages.content:
Sarunyu has a stick of length 1 with one endpoint marked in red. Every minute, he picks one of his sticks uniformly at random and breaks it into two halves of equal length. Compute the expected length of the stick with the red endpoint after 5 minutes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(L_t\) be the length of the stick with the red endpoint after \(t\) minutes, with \(L_0=1\).

After \(t-1\) minutes, there are \(t\) sticks total, and exactly one has the red endpoint. So on minute \(t\), the probability that the red stick is chosen is

\[
\frac{1}{t}.
\]

If it is chosen, its length is halved; if it is not chosen, its length stays the same. Thus, conditional on the past,

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_t \mid L_{t-1}]
=
\frac{1}{t}\cdot \frac{L_{t-1}}{2}
+
\left(1-\frac{1}{t}\right)L_{t-1}
=
\left(1-\frac{1}{2t}\right)L_{t-1}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_5]
=
\prod_{t=1}^{5} \left(1-\frac{1}{2t}\right)
=
\frac12 \cdot \frac34 \cdot \frac56 \cdot \frac78 \cdot \frac9{10}.
\]

This simplifies to

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_5]=\frac{63}{256}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{63}{256}}
\]
